A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 25-page versions of UniGEM. Their main text, tables, figures, equations, and Appendices A–G are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original molecular generation, property prediction, and ablation results in Section 3, with additional BFN, conditional-generation, and representation-learning experiments in Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments, including UniGEM results on QM9 and GEOM-Drugs and the supplementary evaluations in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The two-phase coordinate diffusion, prediction heads, oversampling, branching architecture, and inference procedures are unchanged. The BFN adaptation and conditional-generation procedure in Appendix B already appear in v2.

E1.justification: Both versions cover QM9 molecular generation and six-property prediction, GEOM-Drugs generation, and QM9 property-conditioned generation. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout the reported experiments, including GeoBFN, EquiFM, and GFMDiff in Table 7 and conditional EDM in Table 8. Newly discussed discrete-flow references are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Data splits, model configurations, training budgets, 10,000-molecule evaluation samples, and metrics remain unchanged. Table 8 adds physical-unit labels without changing the reported values or evaluation procedure.

E4.justification: The predictive-loss, sampling/branching, nucleation-time, and shared-layer analyses are retained unchanged in Section 3.2, Figure 2, and Appendix C. No new robustness analysis or case study appears.

E5.justification: Neither version adds or revises run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance testing relative to the other. Table 1 retains identical parenthetical numerical reporting.

E6.justification: Results in Tables 1–9 and Figure 2 are unchanged. For example, UniGEM's QM9 molecule stability remains 89.8% in Table 2, its BFN variant remains at 93.7% in Table 7, and conditional LUMO MAE remains 0.592 in Table 8.

T1.justification: Theorems 2.1–2.2 and the definitions, assumptions, derivations, and proofs in Appendices E–G are unchanged. Appendix F.3 replaces an unresolved citation with Vincent (2011a), without modifying the mathematical argument.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about unified generation and prediction, the two-phase design, improved performance, and potential broader applicability.

C2.justification: The added related-work discussion reiterates the existing rationale for generating coordinates and predicting atom types. Interpretations of results, conditional-evaluation caveats, and limitations on comparisons with alternative molecular generators were already present in v2.

D1.justification: v3 adds a page-1 footnote announcing public code release and providing a repository address; v2 lacks this access disclosure. Implementation, hyperparameter, hardware, and training-time information otherwise remains unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix D.1 adds a focused discussion of discrete-generation methods, including Campbell et al. and Lin et al., contrasting them with UniGEM. Missing citations for GeoBFN and alternative molecular generators are supplied, without changing the overall novelty claim.

P1.justification: The revision adds localized explanatory paragraphs in Appendix D.1 and repairs citation placeholders. The section organization and main narrative remain essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 8 gains a units row and adjusted layout. Added footnote, reference, and related-work text causes page reflow and shifts appendix material, while all six figures and ten tables are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 improves documentation through explicit Table 8 units, repaired citations, a stated code-release link, and clearer positioning relative to discrete-generation methods. The method, empirical evidence, and proofs remain unchanged, so the improvement is limited. A duplicated Vincent reference is a small editorial drawback that does not outweigh these gains.
